clue.text: Quick raising of eyes to angel with cup draw unfolding

indicators.note: unfolding suggests the words opening out and spreading into a new order

explanation.surface: A cherub is pictured beside a cup being pulled out of a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolding' rearranges the letters of ANGEL, CUP and DRAW together.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief look toward the sky or ceiling is a quick lifting of the eyes.

clue.text: See 16 across
100 per cent 24?

parts.note: one hundred per cent of something is all of it
the answer to 24 across is EXACT, which here means correct

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asks whether something is completely spot on.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to the answer EXACT in its sense 'correct'; being entirely correct is a playful reading of the phrase that usually means satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means satisfactory or fine, read here whimsically as wholly correct.

clue.text: 20 2 with a favour to follow?

definitions.meaning: with 20 across this makes the Millennium structure in Greenwich, London
the request '... a favour' splits as two words followed by 'a favour'

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a cross-reference: put 20 across in front and you have the big tent-like building opened in London for the year 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: The building is the Millennium one in Greenwich, and split into two words it opens the phrase asking someone for a favour.

clue.text: Acidic yellow dessert, possible answer to high explosive

definitions.meaning: jelly is slang for gelignite and a lemon is a dud, so a dud stick of gelignite answers the threat of explosives

explanation.surface: A sour yellow pudding is somehow offered as the response to a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: Gelignite is nicknamed 'jelly'; 'lemon' means a failure, so the second reading is a bomb that won't go off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp citrus-flavoured wobbly pudding fits the first reading; a failed gelignite charge fits the second.

clue.text: See 8
Asked for more heart in the end

indicators.note: in places the word for heart inside the word for the end

parts.note: the end is a finish, END
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: Someone longed for more love once things had finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience that calls a performer back demands another number, which is asking for more.

clue.text: Gormley's gone for the halt, then turned

indicators.note: turned tells us to twist these five words round into a new order

explanation.surface: Something of the sculptor's has left for the stop, then turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges GONE FOR THE HALT THEN; Antony Gormley made the huge steel sculpture near Gateshead in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant winged statue near Gateshead is the best-known work by sculptor Antony Gormley.

clue.text: The odd mag, say, concerning a row with the non-drinking Queen about it

annotationWithheld.why: The odd mag, say, concerning a row with the non-drinking Queen about it (7,6): RE + A + DING gives READING, but nothing as held gives the MA of MATTER (only one 'a'); clue looks garbled by OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: The odd mag, say, concerning a row with the non-drinking Queen about it

clue.text: Gangster fitting cowl to chimney

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
lum is the Scottish word for a chimney

explanation.surface: Someone is fixing a cowl to the top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: A chimney cowl is a real hood-shaped cap, which makes the surface look like DIY; LUM is Scots for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug or violent criminal is a gangster.

clue.text: Distance in which vehicle reversed-it's amazing

indicators.note: in which says the distance word has the next piece placed inside it

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: reversed says the vehicle word is read from right to left

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Over a stretch of road a car backed up, which was astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonder or marvel is something astonishing, so 'it's amazing' describes one.

clue.text: Caucasian in a maze? Ridiculous!

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is lost in a labyrinth and finds it absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters of 'maze? Ridiculous' across the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Azerbaijan in the Caucasus region is a Caucasian in the geographical sense.

clue.text: Being overdrawn was an essential part of keeping time

annotationWithheld.why: Being overdrawn was an essential part of keeping time (2,3,3): no wordplay gives the letters from 'was an essential part of keeping time' as held; looks like OCR garble or missing fodder
annotationWithheld.clue: Being overdrawn was an essential part of keeping time

clue.text: Guns surround West African state, unable to wait?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's guns
to ring something is to surround it
Togo is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Artillery encircles a country in West Africa, impatient to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eager to start is impatient and cannot wait.

clue.text: Reach paradise, having made progress without pull

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the progress phrase around the pull word

parts.note: got on means made progress
heave means pull

explanation.surface: Someone gets to heaven having advanced without any influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means 'outside', as in old usage; 'pull' also misleads as influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To die and arrive in heaven is to reach paradise.

clue.text: Paradise and river stick out in Cornwall

parts.note: Eden is both the biblical paradise and a river in Cumbria
to project is to stick out

explanation.surface: A heavenly spot and a river protrude in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only a location: the Eden Project is the large biome garden attraction in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed botanical attraction near St Austell is located in Cornwall, so the location serves as a loose definition.

clue.text: Support less than 4 1/2 gallon cask

parts.note: under means less than
a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons

explanation.surface: A small cask is needed to hold something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to support from below.

clue.text: Light with much more than the usual current?

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large, bigger than usual
amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A light with an unusually heavy current running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device giving light.

clue.text: Old vessel backing into what's essential — fur

indicators.note: into says the turned vessel goes inside the word for essential

parts.note: a must is something essential

indicators.note: backing means the vessel word is read backwards

parts.note: Noah's ark is the old vessel

explanation.surface: An ancient ship reverses into the heart of things, wrapped in fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ARK into KRA, which goes into MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of this North American water rodent is traded as fur, also called musquash.

clue.text: Surrounded by Frenchmen, sick with boredom, moved at last into something fairly new

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the following pieces inside the Frenchmen

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, Frenchmen
ill means sick

indicators.note: moved at last shifts one letter of the boredom word to its end

parts.note: ennui means boredom

explanation.surface: Bored Frenchmen, sick of waiting, finally move into something modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved at last' shifts the U of the boredom word to its end; 'Surrounded by' wraps the Frenchmen round the rest, and the millennium felt new when this was set in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The thousand-year period begun in 2000 was, when the clue was set, a fairly recent event.

clue.text: Setter's a long time on-line with pictures

parts.note: setter's means 'setter is', I'M
an age is a long time
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: The compiler spends ages online with pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on-line' suggests the internet but means on a railway line, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is a collective word for pictures or visual images.

clue.text: Convict in match for most of aircraft

indicators.note: in puts the convict word inside the match word

parts.note: a fusee is a large-headed match
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner takes part in a game for the greater part of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game, but it is the fusee, a windproof match; 'lag' is British slang for a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of an aeroplane is most of the aircraft.

clue.text: Set off high explosive, being supple

parts.note: lit means set off or ignited

explanation.surface: Someone detonates explosives while keeping flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful, the same as supple.

clue.text: Compel payment? Quite correct

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means demand by force; as an adjective it means precise.

clue.text: Good, got shot of American football?

parts.note: rid is the past form: got rid of

explanation.surface: Good to be rid of American football, someone grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The American game is played on a gridiron, which Americans shorten to grid; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang the gridiron game is the grid, short for the gridiron field.

clue.text: Nelson's house not all his entitlement?

indicators.note: not all says the entitlement word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ration is an allowance or entitlement

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson's house is only part of what he is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' trims RATION to RATIO; the admiral's first name is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson's first name was Horatio.

clue.text: Hire middle of field after theatre is full

indicators.note: after says the hire and middle pieces follow the theatre word

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
to let is to hire out

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of field

explanation.surface: Renting the middle of a field after the theatre is sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, completely full.

clue.text: Man left during speed attained by solvers' wheel

indicators.note: during puts the man and left pieces inside the speed word

parts.note: a ton is a speed of 100 mph
he stands for a man
done means attained or achieved
ye is an old word for you, the solvers

explanation.surface: A man going left at speed reaches the solvers' wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ton' is British slang for 100 mph; the wheel is the giant observation wheel on London's South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The large observation wheel by the Thames in London is a wheel.
